macros.name: abslabeldelim
macros.doc: The ⟨text⟩ argument of \abslabeldelim is typeset immediately after the heading.

macros.name: abstitleskip
macros.doc: Without the \abstractrunin declaration, \abstitleskip is aditional vertical space (either positive or negative) that is inserted between the abstract name and the text of the abstract.

macros.name: abstractcol
macros.doc: The \abstractcol declaration specifies that an abstract in a twocolumn class option document should be typeset like a normal, unnumbered chapter.

macros.name: abstractintoc
macros.doc: The \abstractintoc specifies that the abstract title should be added to the ToC.

macros.name: abstractname
macros.doc: \abstractname (default ‘Abstract’) is used as the title for the abstract environment and is set using the \abstractnamefont.

macros.name: abstractnum
macros.doc: The declaration \abstractnum specifies that the abstract should be typeset like a numbered chapter and \abstractrunin specifies that the title of the abstract should look like a run-in heading; these two declarations are mutually exclusive.

macros.name: abstractrunin
macros.doc: The declaration \abstractnum specifies that the abstract should be typeset like a numbered chapter and \abstractrunin specifies that the title of the abstract should look like a run-in heading; these two declarations are mutually exclusive.

macros.name: abstracttextfont
macros.doc: The body of the abstract is typeset using the \abstracttextfont.

macros.name: addappheadtotoc
macros.doc: The command \addappheadtotoc adds an entry to the ToC.

macros.name: added
macros.doc: The \added macro indicates that something has been added to the manuscript and uses ⊕ as its symbol.

macros.name: addtonotes
macros.doc: The macro \addtonotes inserts ⟨text⟩ into the ent file.

macros.name: addtostream
macros.doc: The \addtostream command writes ⟨text⟩ to the output stream ⟨stream⟩, and hence to whatever file is currently attached to the stream.

macros.name: afterchapternum
macros.doc: The macro \afterchapternum is called just after printing a chapter number. By default it inserts \midchapskip space (default 20pt).

macros.name: afterchaptertitle
macros.doc: The macro \afterchaptertitle is called just after printing a chapter title. By default it inserts \afterchapskip space (default 40pt).

macros.name: afterPoemTitle
macros.doc: The macro \afterPoemTitle finishes off the title typesetting.

macros.name: afterPoemTitlenum
macros.doc: \afterPoemTitlenum is called between setting the number and the title. It ends a paragraph (thus making sure any previous \centering is used) and then may add some vertical space.

macros.name: aliaspagestyle
macros.doc: \aliaspagestyle defines the ⟨alias⟩ pagestyle to be the same as the ⟨original⟩ pagestyle.

macros.name: andnext
macros.doc: The class \andnext macro inserts a newline instead of a space.

macros.name: appendix
macros.doc: The \appendix declaration changes the numbering of chapters to an alphabetic form and also changes the names of chapters from \chaptername (default Chapter) to the value of \appendixname (default Appendix).

macros.name: appendixpage
macros.doc: The \appendixpage command generates a part-like page (but no name or number) with the title given by the value of \appendixpagename (default Appendices).

macros.name: arraytostring
macros.doc: The macro \arraytostring assumes that ⟨arrayname⟩ is an array of characters, and defines the macro ⟨result⟩ to be that sequence of characters.

macros.name: AtBeginClass
macros.doc: The \AtBeginClass command will insert ⟨code⟩ just before the ⟨class⟩ class is used.

macros.name: AtBeginFile
macros.doc: The \AtBeginFile macro inserts ⟨code⟩ just before the ⟨filename⟩ file is \input (or \included, etc.).

macros.name: AtBeginPackage
macros.doc: The \AtBeginPackage command will insert ⟨code⟩ just before the ⟨pack⟩ package is used.

macros.name: autocols
macros.doc: The \autocols macro lists its ⟨entries⟩ in columns, proceeding top to bottom and left to right.

macros.name: autorows
macros.doc: The \autorows macro lists the ⟨entries⟩ in rows; that is, the entries are typeset left to right and top to bottom.

macros.name: backmatter
macros.doc: The \backmatter declaration makes no change to the pagination or folios but does prohibit sectional division numbering, and captions, etc., will be numbered continuously.

macros.name: bibintoc
macros.doc: The declaration \bibintoc will cause the thebibliography environment to add the title to the ToC, while the declaration \nobibintoc ensures that the title is not added to the ToC.

macros.name: bibitemsep
macros.doc: In the listing the vertical space between entries is controlled by the length \bibitemsep, which by default is set to the normal \itemsep value.

macros.name: biblistextra
macros.doc: Just at the end of setting up the bibitemlist the \biblistextra command is called. By default this does nothing but you may change it to do something useful.

macros.name: bibname
macros.doc: The value of \bibname (default ‘Bibliography’) is used as the title.

macros.name: bibsection
macros.doc: The macro \bibsection defines the heading for the thebibliography environment; that is, everything before the actual list of items.

macros.name: bicontcaption
macros.doc: Bilingual continuation captions can be typeset via the \bicontcaption command.

macros.name: bitwonumcaption
macros.doc: Bilingual captions can be typeset by the \bitwonumcaption command which has six arguments.

macros.name: book
macros.doc: The \book{⟨title⟩} command puts the book name (default Book), number and ⟨title⟩ on a page by itself.

macros.name: booknamenum
macros.doc: The macro \booknamenum, which is defined to be a space, is called between printing the book name and the number.

macros.name: booknumberline
macros.doc: In the ToC, the macros \booknumberline, \partnumberline and \chapternumberline are responsible respectively for typesetting the \book, \part and \chapter numbers, whereas \numberline does the same for the sectional siblings.

macros.name: bookpageend
macros.doc: The macro \bookpageend finishes off a book title page.

macros.name: bookpagemark
macros.doc: The \book code includes \bookpagemark{⟨title⟩} for capturing the ⟨title⟩ of the book division if it is going to be used, for example, in page headers.

macros.name: booktitlefont
macros.doc: A book’s title is typeset by \printbooktitle using the font specified by \booktitlefont.

macros.name: bottomsectionskip
macros.doc: The length \bottomsectionskip controls the amount of stretch on the short page.

macros.name: boxedverbatiminput
macros.doc: The commands \verbatiminput and \boxedverbatiminput, and their starred versions, act like the verbatim and boxedverbatim environments, except that they get their text from the ⟨file⟩ file.

macros.name: bs
macros.doc: The macro \bs simply prints the ‘\’ backslash.

macros.name: bvbox
macros.doc: Following the \bvbox declaration, a box is drawn round the verbatim text, breaking at page boundaries if necessary; this is the default style.

macros.name: bvnumbersoutside
macros.doc: Line numbers are typeset inside the box after the declaration \bvnumberinside and are typeset outside the box after the declaration \bvnumbersoutside.

macros.name: bvtopandtail
macros.doc: With the \bvtopandtail declaration horizontal lines are drawn at the start and end of the verbatim text, and with the \bvsides declarations, vertical lines are drawn at the left and right of the text.

macros.name: calccentering
macros.doc: After calling \calccentering, ⟨length⟩ is the amount to be added to the spine margin and subtracted from the foredge margin to center the typeblock.

macros.name: cancelthanksrule
macros.doc: Issuing the command \cancelthanksrule will cause the normal \footnoterule definition to be used from thereon; another \usethanksrule command can be issued later if you want to swap back again.

macros.name: captiondelim
macros.doc: The command \captiondelim can be used to change the delimeter.

macros.name: captionnamefont
macros.doc: The ⟨fontspec⟩ specified by \captionnamefont is used for typesetting the caption name; that is, the first part of the caption up to and including the delimeter (e.g., the portion ‘Table 3:’).

macros.name: captionstyle
macros.doc: By default the name and title of a caption are typeset as a block (non-indented) paragraph. \captionstyle can be used to alter this.

macros.name: captiontitlefinal
macros.doc: The argument to \captiontitlefinal is put immediately after the title text but will not appear in the LoF or LoT.

macros.name: captiontitlefont
macros.doc: the ⟨fontspec⟩ specified by \captiontitlefont is used for typesetting the title text of a caption.

macros.name: cardinal
macros.doc: The \cardinal macro is like \fcardinal except that there is no separation between any of the digits.

macros.name: centerfloat
macros.doc: The command \centerfloat is a special version of \center that when used in a wide float will center it with respect to the textblock, i.e., it will extend equally into both margins.

macros.name: centerlastline
macros.doc: \centerlastline style gives a block paragraph but with the last line centered.

macros.name: cftaddnumtitleline
macros.doc: The command \cftaddnumtitleline is similar to \cftaddtitleline except that it also includes ⟨num⟩ as the argument to \numberline.

macros.name: cftaddtitleline
macros.doc: The command \cftaddtitleline will write a \contentsline entry into ⟨ext⟩ for a ⟨kind⟩ entry with title ⟨title⟩ and page number ⟨page⟩.

macros.name: cftdot
macros.doc: The ‘dot’ in a leader is given by the value of \cftdot.

macros.name: cftdotsep
macros.doc: The macro \cftdotsep specifies the default spacing.

macros.name: cftinsertcode
macros.doc: The ⟨code⟩ for the hook is specified via \cftinsertcode where ⟨name⟩ is the name you give to the hook.

macros.name: cftinserthook
macros.doc: The \cftinserthook is somewhat like \addtocontents in that it enables you to insert a code hook into the ToC, etc., where ⟨file⟩ is the (toc, lof, . . . ) file and ⟨name⟩ is the ‘name’ of the hook.

macros.name: cftlocalchange
macros.doc: The command \cftlocalchange will write an entry into the file with extension ⟨ext⟩ to reset the global \@pnumwidth and \@tocrmarg parameter lengths.

macros.name: cftpagenumbersoff
macros.doc: The command \cftpagenumbersoff will eliminate the page numbers for ⟨kind⟩ entries in the listing, where ⟨kind⟩ is the name of one of the standard kinds of entries (e.g., subsection, or figure) or the name of a new entry defined in the document.

macros.name: cftparskip
macros.doc: Normally the \parskip in the ToC, etc., is zero. This may be changed by changing the length \cftparskip.

macros.name: cftsetindents
macros.doc: The command \cftsetindents sets the ⟨kind⟩ entries indent to the length ⟨indent⟩ and its numwidth to the length ⟨numwidth⟩.

macros.name: changecaptionwidth
macros.doc: Issuing the declaration \changecaptionwidth causes the captions to be typeset within a total width ⟨length⟩ as specified by \captionwidth.

macros.name: changed
macros.doc: The macro \changed uses the ⇔ symbol to indicate that something has been changed.

macros.name: changeglossnum
macros.doc: \changeglossnum specifies that ⟨thecounter⟩ should be used to generate the ⟨num⟩ for the ⟨file⟩ glossary.

macros.name: changeglossnumformat
macros.doc: \changeglossnumformat specifies that ⟨format⟩ should be used to format the ⟨num⟩ for the ⟨file⟩ glossary.

macros.name: changeglossref
macros.doc: \changeglossref specifies that ⟨thecounter⟩ should be used to generate the ⟨ref⟩ for the ⟨file⟩ glossary.

macros.name: chapindent
macros.doc: The length \chapindent is provided for use in specifying chapterstyles, but you could use it for any other purposes.

macros.name: chapter
macros.doc: The \chapter command starts a new page and puts the chapter name (default Chapter), number and ⟨title⟩ at the top of the page.

macros.name: chapterheadstart
macros.doc: The macro \chapterheadstart is called just before printing a chapter name and number.

macros.name: chapternamenum
macros.doc: The macro \chapternamenum, which is defined to be a space, is called between printing the chapter name and the number.

macros.name: chapternumberline
macros.doc: In the ToC, the macros \booknumberline, \partnumberline and \chapternumberline are responsible respectively for typesetting the \book, \part and \chapter numbers, whereas \numberline does the same for the sectional siblings.

macros.name: chapterprecis
macros.doc: The command \chapterprecis prints its argument both at the point in the document where it is called, and also adds it to the .toc file.

macros.name: chapterprecishere
macros.doc: The \chapterprecishere macro is intended for use immediately after a \chapter. The ⟨text⟩ argument is typeset in the \precisfont font in a quote environment.

macros.name: chapterprecistoc
macros.doc: The \chapterprecistoc macro puts \precistoctext{⟨text⟩} into the toc file.

macros.name: chapterstyle
macros.doc: The macro \chapterstyle is rather like the \pagestyle command in that it sets the style of any subsequent chapter headings to be ⟨style⟩.

macros.name: chaptitlefont
macros.doc: The title is typeset by \printchaptertitle using the font specified by \chaptitlefont. By default this is a \bfseries font in the \Huge size.

macros.name: checkarrayindex
macros.doc: checks if ⟨arrayname⟩ is an array and if ⟨index⟩ is a valid index for the array. If both conditions hold then \ifbounderror is set false, but if either ⟨arrayname⟩ is not an array or, if it is, ⟨index⟩ is out of range then \ifbounderror is set true.

macros.name: checkifinteger
macros.doc: The command \checkifinteger ckecks if ⟨num⟩ is an integer (not less than zero). If it is then \ifinteger is set true, otherwise it is set false.

macros.name: checkoddpage
macros.doc: The macro \checkoddpage sets \ifoddpage to true if the current page number is odd, otherwise it sets it to false (the page number is even).

macros.name: checkthelayout
macros.doc: The \checkthelayout macro checks the class layout parameters to see whether they have ‘sensible’ values (e.g., the \textwidth is not negative) and, depending on the ⟨algorithm⟩ argument, it may modify the \textheight.

macros.name: citeindexfile
macros.doc: The name of the file for the citation index is stored in the macro \citeindexfile.

macros.name: clearforchapter
macros.doc: The actual macro that sets the opening page for a chapter is \clearforchapter.

macros.name: cleartoevenpage
macros.doc: The \cleartoevenpage command is like \cleardoublepage except that the page following the command will be an even numbered page, and the command takes an optional argument which is applied to the skipped page (if any).

macros.name: cmd
macros.doc: The argument to \cmd should be the name of a macro, including the backslash. It is then printed, using \cmdprint, and also added to the index file with the assumption that ? will be used as the ‘actual’ character (the default is @ which is not of much use if you are trying to index macro names that have @ as part of their names).

macros.name: cmdprint
macros.doc: The argument to \cmdprint should be the name of a macro, including the backslash. It is then printed as is.

macros.name: colorchapnum
macros.doc: The title is set with colorchaptitle and the number with colorchapnum, both of which default to doing nothing.

macros.name: colorchaptitle
macros.doc: The title is set with colorchaptitle and the number with colorchapnum, both of which default to doing nothing.

macros.name: commentsoff
macros.doc: A comment environment ⟨name⟩ may be switched off so that its contents are not ignored by using the \commentsoff declaration.

macros.name: contcaption
macros.doc: The \contcaption command can be used to put a ‘continued’ or ‘concluded’ caption into a float environment.

macros.name: continuousmarks
macros.doc: The \thanks command uses the footnote counter, and normally the counter is zeroed after the titling so that the footnote marks start from 1. If the counter should not be zeroed, then just specify \continuousmarks.

macros.name: continuousnotenums
macros.doc: If you want the numbering to be continuous throughout the document use the \continuousnotenums declaration.

macros.name: contsubbottom
macros.doc: The \contsubcaption, \contsuptop and \contsubbottom commands are the continued versions of the respective subcaptioning commands. These continue the subcaption numbering scheme across (continued) floats.

macros.name: contsubcaption
macros.doc: The \contsubcaption, \contsuptop and \contsubbottom commands are the continued versions of the respective subcaptioning commands. These continue the subcaption numbering scheme across (continued) floats.

macros.name: copypagestyle
macros.doc: The \copypagestyle command creates a new pagestyle called ⟨copy⟩ using the ⟨original⟩ pagestyle specification.

macros.name: cplabel
macros.doc: When strict page checking is used the labels consist of a number preceded by the value of \cplabel, whose default definition is ^_ (e.g., a label may consist of the characters ^_21).

macros.name: createmark
macros.doc: The macro \createmark{⟨sec⟩}{⟨marks⟩}{⟨show⟩}{⟨prefix⟩}{⟨postfix⟩} defines a new macro \⟨sec⟩mark that will take one argument, where ⟨marks⟩ is either left, right or both, ⟨sec⟩ is a sectional division such as part, chapter, section, etc., ⟨show⟩ is one of the terms shownumber, nonumber or notitle.

macros.name: createplainmark
macros.doc: The macro \createplainmark defines the \⟨type⟩mark, where ⟨type⟩ is an unnumbered division-like head, such as toc, lof, index, using ⟨text⟩ as the mark value, and ⟨marks⟩ is left, both or right.

macros.name: cs
macros.doc: The macro \cs prints its argument, putting a backslash in front of it.

macros.name: defaultlists
macros.doc: The open list appearance is used after the \defaultlists declaration is issued.

macros.name: defaultsecnum
macros.doc: The macro \defaultsecnum is a declaration that reverses the effect of \hangsecnum, that is, sectional numbers will be typeset in their familiar places.

macros.name: descriptionlabel
macros.doc: In a description list an \item’s ⟨label⟩ is typeset by descriptionlabel.

macros.name: DisemulatePackage
macros.doc: This command undoes any prior \EmulatedPackage or \EmulatedPackageWithOptions for the ⟨package⟩ package.

macros.name: dropchapter
macros.doc: The command \dropchapter will lower any subsequent chapter titles by ⟨length⟩; a negative ⟨length⟩ will raise the titles.

macros.name: droptitle
macros.doc: The \maketitle command puts the title at a particular height on the page. You can change the vertical position of the title via the length \droptitle.

macros.name: easypagecheck
macros.doc: The simple, but faster, page checking method is used after the \easypagecheck command is issued.

macros.name: emptythanks
macros.doc: The \emptythanks command discards any text from prior use of \thanks.

macros.name: epigraph
macros.doc: The command \epigraph typesets an epigraph using ⟨text⟩ as the main text of the epigraph and ⟨source⟩ being the original author (or book, article, etc.) of the quoted text.

macros.name: epigraphfontsize
macros.doc: The ⟨fontsize⟩ argument to the \epigraphfontsize declaration sets the font size to be used.

macros.name: epigraphforheader
macros.doc: The \epigraphforheader macro takes the same arguments as \epigraphhead but puts ⟨text⟩ into a zero-sized picture at the coordinate position (0,-<distance>); the macro \epigraphpicture holds the resulting picture.

macros.name: epigraphhead
macros.doc: The \epigraphhead macro stores ⟨text⟩ for printing at ⟨distance⟩ below the header on a page.

macros.name: epigraphposition
macros.doc: The horizontal position of an epigraph in relation to the main typeblock is controlled by the ⟨flush⟩ argument to the \epigraphposition declaration.

macros.name: epigraphrule
macros.doc: By default, a rule is drawn between the ⟨text⟩ and ⟨source⟩, with the rule thickness being given by the value of \epigraphrule.

macros.name: epigraphsourceposition
macros.doc: The ⟨flush⟩ argument to the \epigraphsourceposition declaration controls the position of the ⟨source⟩.

macros.name: epigraphtextposition
macros.doc: The ⟨flush⟩ argument to the \epigraphtextposition declaration controls the ⟨text⟩ typesetting style.

macros.name: epigraphwidth
macros.doc: The epigraphs are typeset in a minipage of width \epigraphwidth.

macros.name: fcardinal
macros.doc: The macro \fcardinal prints its ⟨number⟩ argument formatted using \fnumbersep between each triple of digits.

macros.name: feetabovefloat
macros.doc: The standard positioning is used following the \feetabovefloat declaration, which is the default.

macros.name: feetbelowfloat
macros.doc: Following the \feetbelowfloat declaration footnotes will be typeset at the bottom of the page below any bottom floats; they will also be typeset at the bottom of \raggedbottom pages as opposed to being put just after the bottom line of text.

macros.name: firmlist
macros.doc: The command \firmlist or \tightlist can be used immediately after the start of a list environment to reduce the vertical space within that list.

macros.name: firmlists
macros.doc: The spacing following the \firmlists declaration is intermediate between \defaultlists and \tightlists.

macros.name: fixthelayout
macros.doc: The \fixthelayout macro finally implements the layout, making due adjustement for any binding allowance, and calculates the values for all the standard LaTeX layout parameters (such that packages can use these expected values).

macros.name: flagverse
macros.doc: Putting \flagverse at the start of a line will typeset ⟨flag⟩, for example the stanza number, ending at a distance \vleftskip before the line.

macros.name: FloatBlockAllowAbove
macros.doc: \FloatBlockAllowAbove will allow the float to be placed at the top of the same page as \FloatBlock.

macros.name: footfootmark
macros.doc: The class macro for typesetting the marker at the foot of the page is \footfootmark.

macros.name: footmarksep
macros.doc: Second and later lines of the text are offset by the length \footmarksep from the end of the box.

macros.name: footmarkstyle
macros.doc: The appearance of the mark is controlled by \footmarkstyle.

macros.name: footnotesatfoot
macros.doc: \footnotesatfoot (the default) causes \footnote to place its text at the bottom of the page.

macros.name: footparindent
macros.doc: a paragraph within a footnote is indented by \footparindent.

macros.name: footruleheight
macros.doc: The macro \footruleheight is the height of a normal rule above a footer (default zero).

macros.name: footruleskip
macros.doc: \footruleskip is a distance sufficient to ensure that a foot rule will be placed between the bottom of the typeblock and the footer.

macros.name: foottextfont
macros.doc: The text in the footnote is typeset using the \foottextfont font.

macros.name: foottopagenote
macros.doc: you can use \foottopagenote to make \footnote, \footnotemark and \footnotetext works as if it was implemented using end notes.

macros.name: fordinal
macros.doc: The \fordinal macro typesets its ⟨number⟩ argument as a formatted ordinal, using \fnumbersep as the separator.

macros.name: FrameCommand
macros.doc: The frame itself is drawn via the \FrameCommand, which can be changed to obtain other boxing styles.

macros.name: framepichead
macros.doc: The macro \framepichead creates a zero-sized picture that draws a line at the header location, and the macro \framepictextfoot creates a zero-sized picture that draws a line at the footer location and also draws a box around the typeblock.

macros.name: frontmatter
macros.doc: The \frontmatter declaration sets the folios to be printed in lowercase roman numerals, starts the page numbering from i, and prohibits any numbering of sectional divisions.

macros.name: getarrayelement
macros.doc: \getarrayelement sets the parameterless macro ⟨result⟩ to the contents of the ⟨index⟩ location in the ⟨arrayname⟩ array.

macros.name: glossary
macros.doc: Use the \glossary command to add a ⟨term⟩ and its description, ⟨desc⟩, to a glossary file.

macros.name: glossarycolsep
macros.doc: the length \glossarycolsep is the distance between the columns and the length \glossaryrule is the width (default 0) of a vertical rule between the columns.

macros.name: glossaryintoc
macros.doc: The glossary title will be added to the ToC if the \glossaryintoc declaration is in force, but will not be added to the ToC following the \noglossaryintoc.

macros.name: glossarymark
macros.doc: \glossarymark, which by default does nothing, can be redefined to set marks for headers.

macros.name: glossitem
macros.doc: A \glossitem is a glossary entry within a theglossary environment for a ⟨term⟩ with ⟨description⟩.

macros.name: hangcaption
macros.doc: The declaration \hangcaption causes captions to be typeset with the second and later lines of a multiline caption title indented by the width of the caption name.

macros.name: hangpara
macros.doc: Using \hangpara at the start of a paragraph will cause the paragraph to be hung. If the length ⟨indent⟩ is positive the lefthand end of the lines will be indented but if it is negative the righthand ends will be indented by the specified amount.

macros.name: hangsecnum
macros.doc: The macro \hangsecnum is a declaration that makes sectional numbers hang in the margin.

macros.name: hangsubcaption
macros.doc: The \hangsubcaption declaration causes subcaptions to be typeset with the identifier above the title.

macros.name: headnameref
macros.doc: Issuing \headnameref we instead use the header (if available) when preparing the title for the label.

macros.name: headstyles
macros.doc: The default sectional division head styles provided by memoir form the default headstyles and give the same appearance as the standard book and report classes. The set is created via the \makeheadstyles macro and called for via the headstyles declaration.

macros.name: headwidth
macros.doc: The length \headwidth is provided as a (scratch) length that may be used for headers or footers, or any other purpose.

macros.name: hideindexmarks
macros.doc: The \hideindexmarks, which is the default, turns off \showindexmarks.

macros.name: hmpunct
macros.doc: The punctuation between the hours and minutes is \hmpunct which defaults to a colon (:).

macros.name: ifonlyfloats
macros.doc: If the command \ifonlyfloats is issued on a page that contains no text and only floats then the ⟨yes⟩ argument is processed, otherwise on a normal page the ⟨no⟩ argument is processed.

macros.name: IfStreamOpen
macros.doc: The macro \IfStreamOpen checks whether or not the ⟨stream⟩ stream is open. If it is then the ⟨true-code⟩ argument is processed, while when it is not open the ⟨false-code⟩ argument is processed.

macros.name: ignorenoidxfile
macros.doc: Following the declaration \ignorenoidxfile, which is the default, LaTeX will silently pass over attempts to use an idx file which has not been declared via \makeindex.

macros.name: iiirdstring
macros.doc: The ordinal characters are the values of the macros \nthstring (default: th) for most ordinals, \iststring (default: st) for ordinals ending in 1 like 21st , \iindstring (default: nd) for ordinals like 22nd , and \iiirdstring (default: rd) for ordinals like 23rd .

macros.name: iindstring
macros.doc: The ordinal characters are the values of the macros \nthstring (default: th) for most ordinals, \iststring (default: st) for ordinals ending in 1 like 21st , \iindstring (default: nd) for ordinals like 22nd , and \iiirdstring (default: rd) for ordinals like 23rd .

macros.name: indentcaption
macros.doc: The declaration \indentcaption will indent title lines after the first by ⟨length⟩.

macros.name: indentpattern
macros.doc: The indentation pattern for a patverse or patverse* environment is specified via the \indentpattern command, where ⟨digits⟩ is a string of digits (e.g., 3213245281).

macros.name: index
macros.doc: The \index macro specifies that ⟨stuff⟩ is to appear in an index.

macros.name: indexintoc
macros.doc: The declaration \indexintoc will cause the theindex environment to add the title to the ToC, while the declaration \noindexintoc ensures that the title is not added to the ToC.

macros.name: indexname
macros.doc: The index title is given by the current value of \indexname (default ‘Index’).

macros.name: isopage
macros.doc: Robert Bringhurst [Bri99] presented a page layout that was especially suitable for ISO proportioned paper, although it can be applied to any page proportion. The \isopage command implements this design.

macros.name: iststring
macros.doc: The ordinal characters are the values of the macros \nthstring (default: th) for most ordinals, \iststring (default: st) for ordinals ending in 1 like 21st , \iindstring (default: nd) for ordinals like 22nd , and \iiirdstring (default: rd) for ordinals like 23rd .

macros.name: justlastraggedleft
macros.doc: Following the \justlastraggedleft declaration paragraphs will be set justified except the last line will be set raggedleft.

macros.name: killtitle
macros.doc: The \killtitle macro makes all aspects of titling, including \thetitle etc., unavailable from the point that it is issued (using this command will save some macro space if the \thetitle, etc., commands are not required).

macros.name: lastlinerulefill
macros.doc: Using \lastlinerulefill to end a paragraph will cause any spaces at the ends of the lines to be filled with the \lastlineparrule rule.

macros.name: leftcenterright
macros.doc: Following the declaration \leftcenterright paragraphs will be set: First line raggedright, the last line raggedleft, and the remainder centered.

macros.name: leftspringright
macros.doc: The \leftspringright macro sets ⟨ltext⟩ flushleft and raggedright in a column whose width is ⟨lfrac⟩ of the textwidth and, in parallel, it also sets ⟨rtext⟩ raggedleft and flushright in a column that is ⟨rfrac⟩ of the textwidth; the effect is as though there are springs between the lines of the two texts.

macros.name: legend
macros.doc: The \legend command is intended to be used to put an anonymous caption, or legend into a float environment, but may be used anywhere.

macros.name: letcountercounter
macros.doc: At times it is handy to ‘let’ one counter act as if it was a different counter.

macros.name: linenottooshort
macros.doc: Following the \linenottooshort declaration paragraphs will be set as normal, except that the last line will not be shorter than ⟨length⟩ (default 2em).

macros.name: linenumberfont
macros.doc: The \linenumberfont declaration sets ⟨font declaration⟩ as the font for the line numbers.

macros.name: linenumberfrequency
macros.doc: The declaration \linenumberfrequency{⟨nth⟩} will cause every ⟨nth⟩ line of succeeding verses to be numbered.

macros.name: listoffigures
macros.doc: The commands \tableofcontents, \listoffigures and \listoftables typeset, repectively, the Table of Contents (ToC), List of Figures (LoF) and List of Tables (LoT).

macros.name: listoftables
macros.doc: The commands \tableofcontents, \listoffigures and \listoftables typeset, repectively, the Table of Contents (ToC), List of Figures (LoF) and List of Tables (LoT).

macros.name: listtablename
macros.doc: Following LaTeX custom, the title texts are the values of the \contentsname, \listfigurename and \listtablename commands.

macros.name: lxvchars
macros.doc: Based on Table 2.3, the two lengths \xlvchars and \lxvchars are initially set to approximately the lengths of a line of text with 45 or 65 characters, respectively, for Computer Modern Roman in the type size selected for the document.

macros.name: mainmatter
macros.doc: The \mainmatter declaration, which is the default at the start of a document, sets the folios to be printed in arabic numerals, starts the page numbering from 1, and sections and above will be numbered.

macros.name: makechapterstyle
macros.doc: Chapter styles are defined via the \makechapterstyle command, where ⟨style⟩ is the style being defined and ⟨text⟩ is the LaTeX code defining the style.

macros.name: makeevenhead
macros.doc: The macro \makeevenhead defines the ⟨left⟩, ⟨center⟩, and ⟨right⟩ portions of the ⟨style⟩ pagestyle header for even numbered (verso) pages.

macros.name: makeheadposition
macros.doc: The \makeheadposition macro specifies the horizontal positioning of the even and odd headers and footers, respectively, for the ⟨style⟩ pagestyle.

macros.name: makeheadstyles
macros.doc: The default sectional division head styles provided by memoir form the default headstyles and give the same appearance as the standard book and report classes. The set is created via the \makeheadstyles macro and called for via the headstyles declaration.

macros.name: makeindex
macros.doc: In order to make LaTeX collect indexing information the declaration \makeindex must be put in the preamble.

macros.name: makepagestyle
macros.doc: The command \makepagestyle specifies a pagestyle ⟨style⟩ which is initially equivalent to the empty pagestyle.

macros.name: makerunningwidth
macros.doc: The macro \makerunningwidth sets the widths of the ⟨style⟩ pagestyle headers and footers.

macros.name: makethanksmark
macros.doc: The macro \makethanksmark typesets both the thanks marker (via \thanksfootmark) and the thanks text.

macros.name: marg
macros.doc: The macro \marg{⟨arg⟩} prints {⟨arg⟩} for a required argument.

macros.name: maxtocdepth
macros.doc: The class \maxtocdepth command sets the tocdepth counter. It is currently not used in the memoir class.

macros.name: medievalpage
macros.doc: The \medievalpage command generates the position and size of the typeblock according to the principles of medieval scribes and the early printers, as discovered and described by Jan Tschichold [Tsc91].

macros.name: memgobble
macros.doc: The \memgobble macro gobbles down and swallows its argument.

macros.name: memUChead
macros.doc: Defines \memUChead as equivalent to \MakeUppercase.

macros.name: meta
macros.doc: The macro \meta{⟨arg⟩} prints ⟨arg⟩ for an argument to a macro.

macros.name: midbookskip
macros.doc: The macros \midbookskip and \midpartskip are the spacings between the number lines and the titles.

macros.name: midpartskip
macros.doc: The macros \midbookskip and \midpartskip are the spacings between the number lines and the titles.

macros.name: minusname
macros.doc: When a named number is negative, \minusname is put before the spelled out number.

macros.name: movetoevenpage
macros.doc: The \movetoevenpage stops the current page and starts typesetting on the next even numbered page.

macros.name: mpjustification
macros.doc: Basically \mpjustification execute ⟨at left of textblock⟩ when it is executed at the left of the text block and vice versa.

macros.name: namedlegend
macros.doc: As a convenience, the \namedlegend command is like the \caption command except that it does not number the caption and, by default, puts no entry into a ‘List of. . . ’ file.

macros.name: namedsubappendices
macros.doc: If you put the declaration \namedsubappendices before the subappendices environment, the sub-appendix number in the body of the document will be preceded by the value of \appendixname.

macros.name: nametest
macros.doc: The macro \nametest takes two strings as the arguments ⟨str1⟩ and ⟨str2⟩. It sets \ifsamename true if ⟨str1⟩ is the same as ⟨str2⟩, otherwise it sets \ifsamename false.

macros.name: needspace
macros.doc: This macro decides if there is ⟨length⟩ space at the bottom of the current page. If there is, it does nothing, otherwise it starts a new page.

macros.name: Needspace
macros.doc: Like \needspace, the \Needspace macro checks if there is ⟨length⟩ space at the bottom of the current page and if there is not it starts a new page.

macros.name: newarray
macros.doc: \newarray defines the ⟨arrayname⟩ array, where ⟨arrayname⟩ is a name like MyArray. The lowest and highest array indices are set to ⟨low⟩ and ⟨high⟩ respectively, where both are integer numbers.

macros.name: newblock
macros.doc: The \newblock command can be used at appropriate places in the entry for encouraging a linebreak (this is used by the openbib option).

macros.name: newcomment
macros.doc: The class lets you define your own comment environment via the \newcomment command which defines a comment environment called ⟨name⟩.

macros.name: newfixedcaption
macros.doc: The \newfixedcaption command, and its friends, can be used to create or modify a captioning ⟨command⟩ that may be used outside the float environment ⟨float⟩.

macros.name: newfloat
macros.doc: The \newfloat command creates two new floating environments called ⟨fenv⟩ and ⟨fenv*⟩.

macros.name: newfootnoteseries
macros.doc: Calling, say, \newfootnoteseries{Q} creates a set of macros equivalent to those for the normal \footnote but with the ⟨series⟩ appended.

macros.name: newinputstream
macros.doc: The macros \newoutputstream and \newinputstream respectively create a new output and input stream called ⟨stream⟩, where ⟨stream⟩ should be a string of alphabetic characters, like myout or myin.

macros.name: newlistentry
macros.doc: The command \newlistentry creates the commands necessary for typesetting an entry in a ‘List of. . . ’.

macros.name: newlistof
macros.doc: The command \newlistof creates a new ‘List of. . . ’, and assorted commands to go along with it.

macros.name: newoutputstream
macros.doc: The macros \newoutputstream and \newinputstream respectively create a new output and input stream called ⟨stream⟩, where ⟨stream⟩ should be a string of alphabetic characters, like myout or myin.

macros.name: nobibintoc
macros.doc: The declaration \bibintoc will cause the thebibliography environment to add the title to the ToC, while the declaration \nobibintoc ensures that the title is not added to the ToC.

macros.name: nochangemarks
macros.doc: Using \nochangemarks switches off any marking.

macros.name: noDisplayskipStretch
macros.doc: The \noDisplayskipStretch declaration sets the skips back to their normal values.

macros.name: noglossaryintoc
macros.doc: The glossary title will be added to the ToC if the \glossaryintoc declaration is in force, but will not be added to the ToC following the \noglossaryintoc.

macros.name: noindexintoc
macros.doc: The declaration \indexintoc will cause the theindex environment to add the title to the ToC, while the declaration \noindexintoc ensures that the title is not added to the ToC.

macros.name: nopartblankpage
macros.doc: If you use the declaration \nopartblankpage (or \nobookblankpage) then you are responsible for setting everything correctly to end off the \part (or \book) page.

macros.name: noprelistbreak
macros.doc: Putting \noprelistbreak immediately before the \begin{itemize} should prevent a page break.

macros.name: normalcaption
macros.doc: The \normalcaption declaration undoes any previous \hangcaption or \indentcaption declaration.

macros.name: normalcaptionwidth
macros.doc: Issuing the declaration \normalcaptionwidth causes captions to be typeset as normal full width captions.

macros.name: normalsubcaption
macros.doc: The \normalsubcaption declaration, which is the default, undoes any previous \hangsubcaption or \shortsubcaption declaration, so that subcaptions are normally centered.

macros.name: noteidinnotes
macros.doc: The \noteidinnotes calls \idtextinnotes to print the note ⟨id⟩ if it was given as the optional argument to pagenote, otherwise it calls \notenuminnotes to print the note number.

macros.name: notenumintext
macros.doc: The macro \notenumintext is called by \pagenote with the value of the pagenote counter as the ⟨num⟩ argument to print the value of the pagenote counter in the main text.

macros.name: notepageref
macros.doc: Normally the information on which page a note was created is discarded but will be made available to notes in the endnote listing following the \notepageref declaration.

macros.name: nouppercaseheads
macros.doc: Following the declaration \nouppercaseheads the titles in the headings pagestyle will not be automatically uppercased.

macros.name: nthstring
macros.doc: The ordinal characters are the values of the macros \nthstring (default: th) for most ordinals, \iststring (default: st) for ordinals ending in 1 like 21st , \iindstring (default: nd) for ordinals like 22nd , and \iiirdstring (default: rd) for ordinals like 23rd .

macros.name: numtoname
macros.doc: The macro \numtoname typesets its ⟨number⟩ argument using lowercase words.

macros.name: NumToName
macros.doc: The macro \numtoname typesets its ⟨number⟩ argument using lowercase words. The other two macros are similar, except that \numtoName uses uppercase for the initial letter of the first word and \NumToName uses uppercase for the initial letters of all the words.

macros.name: oarg
macros.doc: The macro \oarg{⟨arg⟩} prints [⟨arg⟩] for an optional argument.

macros.name: onecolglossary
macros.doc: The glossary can be typeset in two columns (\twocolglossary) but by default (\onecolglossary) it is set in one column.

macros.name: onecolindex
macros.doc: The index entries are typeset within the theindex environment. By default it is typeset with two columns but following the \onecolindex declaration the environment uses a single column.

macros.name: onecoltocetc
macros.doc: Following the \onecoltocetc declaration, which is the default, the ToC and friends will be set in one column but after the \twocoltocetc declaration they will be set in two columns.

macros.name: onelineskip
macros.doc: The class provides the length \onelineskip which contains the initial leading for the normal font.

macros.name: openinputfile
macros.doc: The command \openinputfile opens the file called ⟨filename⟩ and attaches it to the input stream called ⟨stream⟩ so that it can be read from.

macros.name: openleft
macros.doc: The class options openright, openleft and openany (or their macro equivalents \openright, \openleft and \openany) define \clearforchapter to be respectively (see §18.13) \cleartorecto, \cleartoverso and \clearpage.

macros.name: openoutputfile
macros.doc: The command \openoutputfile opens the file called ⟨filename⟩, either creating it if it does not exist, or emptying it if it already exists.

macros.name: openright
macros.doc: The class options openright, openleft and openany (or their macro equivalents \openright, \openleft and \openany) define \clearforchapter to be respectively (see §18.13) \cleartorecto, \cleartoverso and \clearpage.

macros.name: overridescapmargin
macros.doc: The command \overridescapmargin will force the following caption into the ⟨margin⟩ you specify which can only be left or right.

macros.name: pagenote
macros.doc: In the body of the text use use \pagenote to create an endnote, just as you would use \footnote to create a footnote.

macros.name: pagenotesubhead
macros.doc: The macro \pagenotesubhead typesets the subheadings in an endnote list.

macros.name: pagenumbering
macros.doc: The macros \pagenumbering and \pagenumbering* cause the folios to be printed using the counter representation ⟨rep⟩ for the page number, where ⟨rep⟩ can be one of: Alph, alph, arabic, Roman or roman for uppercase and lowercase letters, arabic numerals, and uppercase and lowercase Roman numerals, respectively.

macros.name: pagetofootnote
macros.doc: \pagetofootnote makes all page notes into footnotes (note that this might not work, because there are places where page notes can be issued but foot notes cannot).

macros.name: paragraphfootnotes
macros.doc: Footnotes are run together as a single paragraph after the \paragraphfootnotes declaration.

macros.name: parg
macros.doc: The macro \parg{⟨arg⟩} prints (⟨arg⟩) for a parenthesized argument.

macros.name: parnopar
macros.doc: The macro \parnopar forces a new paragraph but without appearing to (the first line in the following paragraph follows immediately after the last element in the prior paragraph with no line break).

macros.name: partname
macros.doc: Prints the part name (\partname) using the \partnamefont.

macros.name: partnamenum
macros.doc: The macro \partnamenum, which is defined to be a space, is called between printing the part name and the number.

macros.name: partnumberline
macros.doc: In the ToC, the macros \booknumberline, \partnumberline and \chapternumberline are responsible respectively for typesetting the \book, \part and \chapter numbers, whereas \numberline does the same for the sectional siblings.

macros.name: pfbreakdisplay
macros.doc: The fancy break, which takes the same vertical space, is given by the ⟨text⟩ argument of \pfbreakdisplay.

macros.name: pfbreakskip
macros.doc: The gap for the plain break is given by the length \pfbreakskip which is initialised to produce two blank lines.

macros.name: plainbreak
macros.doc: The \plainbreak is an anonymous division. It puts ⟨num⟩ blank lines into the typescript and the first line of the following paragraph is not indented.

macros.name: plainfancybreak
macros.doc: If there is text on the page and enough space left to put some text after a break the \plainfancybreak command will use a \plainbreak with ⟨num⟩ lines, otherwise (the break would come at the top or bottom of the page) it will use a \fancybreak with ⟨text⟩.

macros.name: PoemTitleheadstart
macros.doc: As defined, \PoemTitleheadstart inserts vertical space before a poem title.

macros.name: poemtitlemark
macros.doc: The macro \poemtitlemark is called with the argument ⟨forhead⟩ so that it may be used to set marks for use in a page header via the normal mark process.

macros.name: poemtitlepstyle
macros.doc: The \poemtitlepstyle macro, which by default does nothing, is provided as a hook so that, for example, it can be redefined to specify a particular pagestyle that should be used.

macros.name: poemtoc
macros.doc: The kind of entry made in the ToC by \PoemTitle is defined by \poemtoc.

macros.name: postcaption
macros.doc: The commands \precaption and \postcaption specify ⟨pretext⟩ and ⟨posttext⟩ that will be processed at the start and end of a caption.

macros.name: postnotetext
macros.doc: The actual text part of the page note is enclosed by \prenotetext and postnotetext.

macros.name: precaption
macros.doc: The commands \precaption and \postcaption specify ⟨pretext⟩ and ⟨posttext⟩ that will be processed at the start and end of a caption.

macros.name: prechapterprecisshift
macros.doc: The length \prechapterprecisshift controls the vertical spacing before a \chapterprecis.

macros.name: prenoteinnotes
macros.doc: At the start and end we have the two macros \prenoteinnotes and \postnoteinnotes, they take care of preparing for and ending an entry in the list.

macros.name: prenotetext
macros.doc: The actual text part of the page note is enclosed by \prenotetext and postnotetext.

macros.name: printbookname
macros.doc: The macro \printbookname typesets the book name (the value of \bookname) using the font specified by \booknamefont.

macros.name: printbooknum
macros.doc: the book number is typeset by \printbooknum using the font specified by \booknumfont, which has the same default as \booknamefont.

macros.name: printbooktitle
macros.doc: A book’s title is typeset by \printbooktitle using the font specified by \booktitlefont.

macros.name: printchaptername
macros.doc: The macro \printchaptername typesets the chapter name (default Chapter or Appendix) using the font specified by \chapnamefont.

macros.name: printchapternonum
macros.doc: The macro \printchapternonum is called just before an unnumbered chapter title text is typeset.

macros.name: printchapternum
macros.doc: the chapter number is typeset by \printchapternum using the font specified by \chapnumfont, which has the same default as \chapnamefont.

macros.name: printchaptertitle
macros.doc: The title is typeset by \printchaptertitle using the font specified by \chaptitlefont.

macros.name: printglossary
macros.doc: To print a glossary call \printglossary which will print the glossary from file \jobname.gls, or from file.gls if the optional argument is used.

macros.name: printindex
macros.doc: The \printindex command will print an index where by default the indexed items are assumed to be in a file called jobname.ind.

macros.name: printpagenotes
macros.doc: The \printpagenotes macro inputs the ent endnote file for printing and then closes it to any further notes. For notes at the end of each chapter put \printpagenotes*, which inputs the ent file for printing then empties it ready for more notes, at the end of each chapter.

macros.name: printpartname
macros.doc: the macro \printpartname typesets the part name (the value of \partname) using the font specified by \partnamefont.

macros.name: printpartnum
macros.doc: the part number is typeset by \printpartnum using the font specified by \partnumfont, which has the same default as \partnamefont.

macros.name: printparttitle
macros.doc: a part’s title is typeset by \printparttitle using the font specified by \parttitlefont.

macros.name: printPoemTitlenonum
macros.doc: If the title is unnumbered then \printPoemTitlenonum is used instead of the \printPoemTitlenum and \afterPoemTitlenum pair of macros.

macros.name: printPoemTitlenum
macros.doc: \printPoemTitlenum typesets the number for a poem title.

macros.name: provideenvironment
macros.doc: The macros \provideenvironment, \providelength and \providecounter take the same arguments as their \new... counterparts. If the environment, length or counter has not been defined then it is defined accordingly, otherwise the macros do nothing except produce a warning message for information purposes.

macros.name: providelength
macros.doc: The macros \provideenvironment, \providelength and \providecounter take the same arguments as their \new... counterparts. If the environment, length or counter has not been defined then it is defined accordingly, otherwise the macros do nothing except produce a warning message for information purposes.

macros.name: raggedbottomsection
macros.doc: The \raggedbottomsection declaration will typeset any pages that are short because of a moved subhead as though \raggedbottom was in effect for the short page; other pages are not affected.

macros.name: raggedrightthenleft
macros.doc: Following the declaration \raggedrightthenleft paragraphs will be set with the first line raggedright and the remainder set raggedleft.

macros.name: raggedyright
macros.doc: Text set \raggedyright usually fills more of the available width and paragraphs are indented by \ragrparindent, which is initially set to \parindent.

macros.name: readaline
macros.doc: The \readaline reads what TeX considers to be one line from the file that is currently associated with the input stream ⟨stream⟩.

macros.name: readboxedverbatim
macros.doc: \readverbatim and \readboxedverbatim get their text from the file currently attached to the ⟨stream⟩ input stream.

macros.name: readstream
macros.doc: The command \readstream reads the entire contents of the file currently associated with the input stream ⟨stream⟩.

macros.name: readverbatim
macros.doc: \readverbatim and \readboxedverbatim get their text from the file currently attached to the ⟨stream⟩ input stream.

macros.name: renewleadpage
macros.doc: The macro \renewleadpage redefines an existing leadpage command.

macros.name: reportnoidxfile
macros.doc: After the declaration \reportnoidxfile LaTeX will whine about any attempts to write to an unopened file.

macros.name: RequireAtEndClass
macros.doc: The \RequireAtEndClass command will, like \AtEndClass, insert ⟨code⟩ at the end of the ⟨class⟩ class if it has not yet been used. If the class has already been used then the ⟨code⟩ is called immediately.

macros.name: RequireAtEndPackage
macros.doc: The \RequireAtEndPackage command will, like \AtEndPackage, insert ⟨code⟩ at the end of the ⟨pack⟩ package if it has not yet been used. If the package has already been used then the ⟨code⟩ is called immediately.

macros.name: restorepagenumber
macros.doc: The macro \savepagenumber saves the current page number, and the macro \restorepagenumber sets the page number to the saved value.

macros.name: russianpar
macros.doc: Ending a paragraph with \russianpar causes it to be set following Russian typographic rules.

macros.name: savepagenumber
macros.doc: The macro \savepagenumber saves the current page number, and the macro \restorepagenumber sets the page number to the saved value.

macros.name: saythanks
macros.doc: The command \saythanks ensures that any \thanks texts from an earlier \maketitle are printed out as normal.

macros.name: see
macros.doc: The \see command replaces the page number by the phrase ‘see ⟨text⟩’, while the \seealso command adds ‘see also ⟨text⟩’ to the entry.

macros.name: setarrayelement
macros.doc: The \setarrayelement macro sets the ⟨index⟩ location in the ⟨arrayname⟩ array to be ⟨text⟩.

macros.name: setbiblabel
macros.doc: The style of the labels marking the bibliographic entries can be set via \setbiblabel.

macros.name: setbinding
macros.doc: In some cases, for example when doing a Japanese stab binding, it may be desireable to add a small allowance to the spine margin for the binding. You can use the command \setbinding for this purpose.

macros.name: setbvlinenums
macros.doc: The \setbvlinenums macro can be used to specify that the number of the first line of the following boxedverbatim shall be ⟨first⟩ and the first printed number shall be ⟨startat⟩.

macros.name: setcftvspacecmd
macros.doc: This macro can set the vertical spacing command used by \chapter and the friends that stem from \newlistentry.

macros.name: setcolsepandrule
macros.doc: The macro \setcolsepandrule sets the gutter width, \columnsep, to ⟨colsep⟩ and the thickness of the rule, \columnseprule, to ⟨thickness⟩.

macros.name: setDisplayskipStretch
macros.doc: The declaration \setDisplayskipStretch will increase the before and after displayskips by ⟨fraction⟩, which must be at least 0.0.

macros.name: setfloatlocations
macros.doc: You can set the location for all floats of type ⟨float⟩ to ⟨locs⟩ with the \setfloatlocations declaration.

macros.name: sethangfrom
macros.doc: The \sethangfrom macro redefines \@hangfrom to be ⟨code⟩.

macros.name: setheaderspaces
macros.doc: The macro \setheaderspaces is for specifying the spacing above and below the page header.

macros.name: setheadfoot
macros.doc: The \setheadfoot macro sets the \headheight parameter to the value ⟨headheight⟩ and the \footskip parameter to ⟨footskip⟩.

macros.name: setlrmarginsandblock
macros.doc: The command \setlrmarginsandblock can be used to specify the spine and fore-edge margins, where the page width is fixed and the width of the typeblock depends on the margins.

macros.name: setmarginfloatcaptionadjustment
macros.doc: The intent is to enable the user to choose a different captioning style (or similar) within a margin float, for example typesetting the caption ragged left/right depending on the page.

macros.name: setmarginnotes
macros.doc: The command \setmarginnotes sets the parameters for marginal notes.

macros.name: setpnumwidth
macros.doc: The command \setpnumwidth can be used to change the width of the box (LaTeX ’s internal \@pnumwidth).

macros.name: setsecheadstyle
macros.doc: The macro \setsecheadstyle lowercases the title and typesets it small caps.

macros.name: setsecnumdepth
macros.doc: Instead of having to remember the levels if you want to change what gets numbered you can use the \setsecnumdepth command. It sets secnumdepth so that divisions ⟨secname⟩ and above will be numbered.

macros.name: setsidebarheight
macros.doc: The command \setsidebarheight sets the height of sidebars to ⟨height⟩, without making any allowance for \sidebartopsep.

macros.name: setsidebars
macros.doc: The \setsidebars command can be used to set the sidebar parameters.

macros.name: setsidecappos
macros.doc: By default a sidecaption is vertically centered with respect to the float it is captioning. This can be altered by using the \setsidecappos declaration.

macros.name: setsidefootheight
macros.doc: \setsidefootheight sets the maximal height of the side footnote column, default textwidth.

macros.name: setSingleSpace
macros.doc: The \setSingleSpace command is meant to be used to adjust slightly the normal spacing betwen lines, perhaps because the font being used looks too crampled or loose. The effect is that the normal \baselineskip spacing will be multiplied by ⟨factor⟩, which should be close to 1.0.

macros.name: setstocksize
macros.doc: If you have some other size that you want to use, the command \setstocksize can be used to specify that the stock size is ⟨height⟩ by ⟨width⟩.

macros.name: setsubsecheadstyle
macros.doc: The title is typeset (\setsubsecheadstyle) raggedright in a normal sized italic font.

macros.name: settitlingpagenumbering
macros.doc: The macro \settitlingpagenumbering can be used to control how \thepage is configured inside a titlingpage.

macros.name: settocdepth
macros.doc: The value of the tocdepth counter can be changed by using \setcounter or \settocdepth.

macros.name: settrimmedsize
macros.doc: The command \settrimmedsize can be used to specify the height and width of the page (after any trimming).

macros.name: settrims
macros.doc: The command \settrims can be used to specify the amount intended to be removed from the top (⟨top⟩) and fore-edge (⟨foredge⟩) of the stock material to produce the top and foreedge of a recto page.

macros.name: settypeblocksize
macros.doc: The command \settypeblocksize is similar to \settrimmedsize except that it sets the \textheight and \textwidth for the typeblock.

macros.name: settypeoutlayoutunit
macros.doc: By using the macro \settypeoutlayoutunit, the user can change the unit in which the layout list is shown.

macros.name: setulmarginsandblock
macros.doc: The command \setulmarginsandblock can be used to specify the upper and lower margins, where the page height is fixed and the height of the typeblock depends on the margins.

macros.name: setverbatimfont
macros.doc: The default font for verbatims is the normal sized monospaced font. The declaration can be used to specify a different font.

macros.name: setverselinenums
macros.doc: The \setverselinenums macro can be used to specify that the number of the first line of the following verse shall be ⟨first⟩ and the first printed number shall be ⟨startat⟩.

macros.name: shortsubcaption
macros.doc: Following the \shortsubcaption declaration subcaptions that are less than a full line in length are typeset left justified instead of centered.

macros.name: showheadfootlocoff
macros.doc: Following the declaration \showheadfootlocoff the macros \framepichead and \framepictextfoot do not draw lines showing the header and footer locations.

macros.name: showindexmarks
macros.doc: The declaration \showindexmarks causes the argument to practically any \index and \specialindex to be printed in the margin of the page where the indexing command was issued.

macros.name: showtrimsoff
macros.doc: If the showtrims class option has been used then the \showtrimsoff declaration switches off the trim marks; the \showtrimson declaration, which is the default, switches on the trim marks.

macros.name: showtrimson
macros.doc: If the showtrims class option has been used then the \showtrimsoff declaration switches off the trim marks; the \showtrimson declaration, which is the default, switches on the trim marks.

macros.name: sidebar
macros.doc: The \sidebar command is like \marginpar in that it sets the ⟨text⟩ in the margin. However, unlike \marginpar the ⟨text⟩ will start near the top of the page, and may continue onto later pages if it is too long to go on a single page.

macros.name: sidebarhsep
macros.doc: The ⟨text⟩ of a \sidebar is typeset in a column of width \sidebarwidth and there is a horizontal gap of \sidebarhsep between the main text and the sidebar.

macros.name: sidebarmargin
macros.doc: The macro \sidebarmargin{⟨placement⟩} can be used to specify which margin the side note should go to.

macros.name: sidebartopsep
macros.doc: The length \sidebartopsep controls the vertical position of the top of a sidebar.

macros.name: sidebarvsep
macros.doc: The length \sidebarvsep is the vertical gap between sidebars that fall on the same page; it also has a role in controlling the start of sidebars with respect to the top of the page.

macros.name: sidebarwidth
macros.doc: The ⟨text⟩ of a \sidebar is typeset in a column of width \sidebarwidth and there is a horizontal gap of \sidebarhsep between the main text and the sidebar.

macros.name: sidecapraise
macros.doc: The caption will be raised by the length \sidecapraise in addition to the calculated movement (or lowered if \sidecapraise is negative).

macros.name: sidecapsep
macros.doc: The caption is set in a box \sidecapwidth wide (the default is \marginparwidth) offset \sidecapsep (default \marginparsep) into the margin.

macros.name: sidecapstyle
macros.doc: Just before the caption is set, the \sidecapstyle command is called. This may be used to set the styling for the particular caption.

macros.name: sidecapwidth
macros.doc: The caption is set in a box \sidecapwidth wide (the default is \marginparwidth) offset \sidecapsep (default \marginparsep) into the margin.

macros.name: sidefootmarksep
macros.doc: Second and later lines of the text are offset by the length \sidefootmarksep from the end of the box.

macros.name: sidefootmarkwidth
macros.doc: The mark is typeset in a box of width \sidefootmarkwidth If this is negative, the mark is outdented into the margin, if zero the mark is flush left, and when positive the mark is indented.

macros.name: sidefootparindent
macros.doc: The first line of a paragraph within a footnote is indented by \sidefootparindent.

macros.name: sidepar
macros.doc: The \sidepar macro is similar to \marginpar except that it produces side notes that do not float — they may overlap.

macros.name: sideparfont
macros.doc: The command \sideparfont is used to specify the font used for the \sidepar, default is \normalfont\normalsize.

macros.name: sideparmargin
macros.doc: The macro \sideparmargin{⟨placement⟩} can be used to specify which margin the side note should go to.

macros.name: sideparvshift
macros.doc: The length \sideparvshift can be used to make vertical adjustments to the position of \sidepar notes.

macros.name: SingleSpacing
macros.doc: The declaration \SingleSpacing returns everthing to normal, or at least the setting from \setSingleSpace if it has been used.

macros.name: slashfrac
macros.doc: The class provides the \slashfrac command which typesets its arguments like 3/4. Unlike the \frac command which can only be used in math mode, the \slashfrac command can be used in text and math modes.

macros.name: sloppybottom
macros.doc: The declaration \sloppybottom lets TeX put an extra line at the bottom of a page to avoid a widow on the following page.

macros.name: sourceatright
macros.doc: Using \sourceatright at the end of the quotation will typeset ⟨text⟩ flushright at the end of the line if there is enough space, otherwise it typesets it flushright on the next line.

macros.name: stanzaskip
macros.doc: The vertical space between stanzas is the length \stanzaskip.

macros.name: strictpagecheck
macros.doc: Odd/even page checking may be either strict (\strictpagecheck) or easy (or one might call it lazy) (\easypagecheck). Easy checking works most of the time but if it fails at any point then the strict checking should be used.

macros.name: stringtoarray
macros.doc: The macro \stringtoarray puts each character from ⟨string⟩ sequentially into the ⟨arrayname⟩ array, starting at index 1.

macros.name: subbottom
macros.doc: The \subbottom command is identical to \subtop except that the identifier, and potentially the ⟨subtitle⟩, is placed below the ⟨text⟩.

macros.name: subcaptionfont
macros.doc: The size of the font used for subcaptions is specified by \subcaptionsize, and the fonts for the identifier and text are specified by \subcaptionlabelfont for the identifier and by \subcaptionfont for the title text.

macros.name: subcaptionref
macros.doc: If the \subcaptionref macro is used instead of \ref then only the subcaption identifier is printed.

macros.name: subcaptionsize
macros.doc: The size of the font used for subcaptions is specified by \subcaptionsize, and the fonts for the identifier and text are specified by \subcaptionlabelfont for the identifier and by \subcaptionfont for the title text.

macros.name: subconcluded
macros.doc: The \subconcluded command is used to indicate that the continued (sub) float has been concluded and the numbering scheme is reinitialized.

macros.name: subitem
macros.doc: A \item command flags a main entry; a subentry of a main entry is indicated by \subitem and a subentry of a subentry is flagged by \subsubitem.

macros.name: subsubitem
macros.doc: A \item command flags a main entry; a subentry of a main entry is indicated by \subitem and a subentry of a subentry is flagged by \subsubitem.

macros.name: subtop
macros.doc: The command \subtop puts a subcaption identifier on top of ⟨contents⟩.

macros.name: symbolthanksmark
macros.doc: Just for convenience the \symbolthanksmark command sets the series to be footnote symbols.

macros.name: tableofcontents
macros.doc: The commands \tableofcontents, \listoffigures and \listoftables typeset, repectively, the Table of Contents (ToC), List of Figures (LoF) and List of Tables (LoT).

macros.name: thanksfootmark
macros.doc: A thanks mark in the footnote region is typeset by \thanksfootmark.

macros.name: thanksheadextra
macros.doc: The \thanksheadextra command will insert ⟨pre⟩ and ⟨post⟩ before and after the thanks markers in the titling block.

macros.name: thanksmark
macros.doc: The command \thanksmark{⟨n⟩} is similar to \footnotemark[⟨n⟩] in that it prints a thanks mark identical to that of the ⟨n⟩’th \thanks command.

macros.name: thanksmarksep
macros.doc: The value of the length \thanksmarksep controls the indentation the second and subsequent lines of the thanks text, with respect to the end of the mark box.

macros.name: thanksmarkseries
macros.doc: Any \thanks are marked with symbols in the titling and footnotes. The command \thanksmarkseries can be used to change the marking style.

macros.name: thanksmarkwidth
macros.doc: The thanks mark in the footnote is typeset right justified in a box of width \thanksmarkwidth.

macros.name: thanksrule
macros.doc: \thanksrule is initialised to be a copy of \footnoterule as it is defined at the end of the preamble.

macros.name: theauthor
macros.doc: The class provides the \thetitle, \theauthor and \thedate commands that can be used for printing these elements of the title later in the document, if desired.

macros.name: thedate
macros.doc: The class provides the \thetitle, \theauthor and \thedate commands that can be used for printing these elements of the title later in the document, if desired.

macros.name: thetitle
macros.doc: The class provides the \thetitle, \theauthor and \thedate commands that can be used for printing these elements of the title later in the document, if desired.

macros.name: threecolumnfootnotes
macros.doc: Following the \twocolumnfootnotes declaration footnotes will be typeset in two columns, and similarly they are typeset in three columns after the \threecolumnfootnotes declaration.

macros.name: tightlists
macros.doc: After the declaration \tightlists is issued, the extra vertical spacing between the list items is deleted.

macros.name: titleref
macros.doc: The macro \titleref is a class addition to the usual set of cross referencing commands. Instead of printing a number it typesets the title associated with the labelled number.

macros.name: tmarkbm
macros.doc: The pictures \tmarktm, \tmarkmr, \tmarkbm, and \tmarkml are placed at the top middle, middle right, bottom middle and middle left of the edges of the page.

macros.name: tmarkml
macros.doc: The pictures \tmarktm, \tmarkmr, \tmarkbm, and \tmarkml are placed at the top middle, middle right, bottom middle and middle left of the edges of the page.

macros.name: tmarktm
macros.doc: The pictures \tmarktm, \tmarkmr, \tmarkbm, and \tmarkml are placed at the top middle, middle right, bottom middle and middle left of the edges of the page.

macros.name: trimLmarks
macros.doc: The declaration \trimLmarks calls for corner marks in the shape of an ‘L’, in various orientations depending on the particular corner.

macros.name: trimmarks
macros.doc: The \trimmarks macro is responsible for displaying up to 8 marks.

macros.name: trimmarkscolor
macros.doc: The macro \trimmarkscolor is despite its name a normal (empty) macro. By redefining it one can change the color of the trimmarks, handy for example if the document has a dark background color.

macros.name: trimNone
macros.doc: The declaration \trimNone disables all kinds of trim marking.

macros.name: trimXmarks
macros.doc: After the declaration \trimXmarks marks in the shape of a cross are placed at the four corners of the page.

macros.name: twocolglossary
macros.doc: The glossary can be typeset in two columns (\twocolglossary) but by default (\onecolglossary) it is set in one column.

macros.name: twocolindex
macros.doc: The default two column behaviour is restored after the \twocolindex declaration.

macros.name: twocoltocetc
macros.doc: Following the \onecoltocetc declaration, which is the default, the ToC and friends will be set in one column but after the \twocoltocetc declaration they will be set in two columns.

macros.name: twocolumnfootnotes
macros.doc: Following the \twocolumnfootnotes declaration footnotes will be typeset in two columns, and similarly they are typeset in three columns after the \threecolumnfootnotes declaration.

macros.name: typeoutlayout
macros.doc: writes the current class layout parameter values to the terminal and the log file.

macros.name: typeoutstandardlayout
macros.doc: The macro \typeoutstandardlayout writes the standard layout parameter values to the terminal and log file so that you can compare the two sets of parameter values.

macros.name: uppercaseheads
macros.doc: The default is \uppercaseheads which specifies that the titles are to be automatically uppercased.

macros.name: verselinebreak
macros.doc: Using \verselinebreak will cause later text in the line to be typeset indented on the following line.

macros.name: verselinenumbersleft
macros.doc: The \verselinenumbersleft declaration will set any subsequent line numbers to the left of the lines.

macros.name: verselinenumbersright
macros.doc: Following the declaration \verselinenumbersright, which is the default, any verse line numbers will be set in the righthand margin.

macros.name: vin
macros.doc: The command \vin is shorthand for \hspace*{\vgap} for use at the start of an indented line of verse.

macros.name: vinphantom
macros.doc: The macro \vinphantom can be used at the start of a line to give an indentation as though the line started with ⟨text⟩.

macros.name: vleftmargin
macros.doc: For the class’s version of verse the default indent is set by the length \vleftmargin (which is initially set to leftmargini).

macros.name: vrightskip
macros.doc: The numbers are set at a distance \vrightskip (default 1em) into the margin.

macros.name: xlvchars
macros.doc: Sets \xlvchars to the length of 45 characters in the ⟨fontspec⟩ font (default \normalfont).

envs.name: adjustwidth
envs.doc: The adjustwidth environment temporarily adds the length ⟨left⟩ to the lefthand margin and ⟨right⟩ to the righthand margin.

envs.name: appendices
envs.doc: The appendices environment acts like the \appendix command in that it resets the numbering and naming of chapters.

envs.name: boxedverbatim
envs.doc: The boxedverbatim and boxedverbatim* environments are like the verbatim and verbatim* environments except that a box, allowing page breaks, may be put around the verbatim text and the lines of text may be numbered.

envs.name: ctabular
envs.doc: The ctabular environment is similar to tabular, but with a couple of differences, the main one being that the table will merrily continue across page breaks.

envs.name: epigraphs
envs.doc: The epigraphs environment typesets a list of epigraphs, and by default places them at the right hand side of the typeblock.

envs.name: fboxverbatim
envs.doc: The fboxverbatim environment typesets its contents verbatim and puts a tightly fitting frame around the result; in a sense it is similar to the \fbox command.

envs.name: flexlabelled
envs.doc: The flexlabelled environment adds additional controls to the labelled one.

envs.name: framed
envs.doc: The framed environment delineates the box by drawing a rectangular frame.

envs.name: hangparas
envs.doc: The hangparas environment is like the \hangpara command except that every paragraph in the environment will be hung.

envs.name: labelled
envs.doc: The labelled environment is like the description environment except that you can specify the label format via the ⟨name⟩ argument where \name is the formatting macro.

envs.name: leftbar
envs.doc: The leftbar environment draws a thick vertical line at the left of the text.

envs.name: shaded
envs.doc: The shaded environment typesets the box with a shaded or colored background.

envs.name: sidecontcaption
envs.doc: Sidecaptions may be continued with the sidecontcaption environment.

envs.name: sidelegend
envs.doc: Legends may be set at the side with the sidelegend environment.

envs.name: sidenamedlegend
envs.doc: Named legends may be set at the side with the sidenamedlegend environment.

envs.name: subappendices
envs.doc: The subappendices environment can be used to put appendices at the end of a chapter.

envs.name: thebibliography
envs.doc: The environment takes one required argument, ⟨exlabel⟩, which is a piece of text as wide as the widest label in the bibliography.

envs.name: theglossary
envs.doc: Glossary entries are typeset in a theglossary environment.

envs.name: theindex
envs.doc: The index entries are typeset within the theindex environment.

envs.name: verbatimoutput
envs.doc: The text within a verbatimoutput environment is written verbatim to the ⟨file⟩ file.

envs.name: vplace
envs.doc: The contents of the vplace environment are vertically centered.
